proposal: The Mandate says the next Administration arguably should place its nominees in acting roles in similar positions while they await confirmation, such as serving as senior official performing the duties of the CBP Commissioner. It recommends legislation removing the confirmation requirement from lower-level DHS posts, including FEMA posts other than the Administrator, and setting a durable, politically oriented line of succession in which a career employee holding a leadership post is treated as vacant for succession purposes and acting Secretaries have explicit authority to finalize agency actions.

status_summary: On 2025-01-20 Executive Order 14148 revoked the prior administration's Executive Order 14135 of 2025-01-03, which had set an order of succession within DHS running through the TSA Administrator, the Under Secretary for Intelligence and Analysis, the FLETC Director and the FEMA Region 3 Administrator; no replacement DHS succession order was found in the Federal Register. By 2025-02-18 Pete Flores was serving as Acting Commissioner of CBP, per a CBP news release. Acting leadership has continued at DHS components: news reports state that ICE has had no Senate-confirmed director since 2017 and that on 2026-05-13 DHS named a new acting leader to replace the outgoing acting director, that FEMA had an acting head from 2025-05-08, and that TSA had an acting administrator from April 2025 until a Senate-confirmed administrator was sworn in (reported 2026-08-11). No bill on DHS succession or on removing Senate confirmation from DHS posts was found; one general bill on presidential power, S. 2838 (Protecting Our Democracy Act), has been in committee since 2025-09-17 with no later action, so the legislative parts remain unaddressed.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14148 was signed and, in section 2(kkk), revoked Executive Order 14135 of 2025-01-03, which had provided an order of succession within DHS.
A CBP news release of this date quotes Pete Flores as Acting Commissioner of CBP; the release gives no start date for the role.

David Richardson became acting head of FEMA, as senior official performing the duties of the Administrator, on the day the prior head was removed; he resigned on 2025-11-17 and the FEMA chief of staff was to take over on 2025-12-01. The report does not show a nominee placed as an acting official.

A DHS spokesperson said David Venturella would lead ICE on an acting basis, replacing the outgoing acting director, who was to leave by 2026-05-31; the report states ICE has had no Senate-confirmed director since 2017.

title: Use acting officials, set a political line of succession, cut Senate-confirmed DHS posts
uncertainties: Executive Order 14135, revoked by Executive Order 14148 (Sec. 2(kkk), confirmed on federalregister.gov), was itself an order of succession that revoked EO 13753 and struck section 88 of EO 13286, and it does not mention career employees; it was re-read in review on 2026-10-18. Whether DHS issued a replacement order was not found in Federal Register API queries since 2025-01-20 (researcher: order of succession and Homeland Security, one result, EO 14148 itself; review: presidential documents on succession and the Secretary of Homeland Security, 0 results), so the revocation may only return DHS to the statutory default and is not shown to match the Mandate's political-only succession. The Federal Register pages were read through a summarizing tool. The CBP acting role rests on a CBP news release of 2025-02-18 and an undated House Appropriations hearing biography, which give the title Acting Commissioner and no start date; the biography describes him as the agency's senior career official, but whether the role began on 2025-01-20 was not confirmed, and a memorandum on ending catch and release that he is said to have signed was not found in any opened document. News articles opened on 2026-10-22 (govexec.com, wghn.com, travelweekly.com) show acting leaders at ICE (successor named 2026-05-13), FEMA (from 2025-05-08) and TSA (from April 2025, ended by a Senate-confirmed administrator reported 2026-08-11); none describes a nominee placed as an acting official, so use of actings is a parallel executive practice and not shown to be the Mandate's nominee-as-acting method. Whether the ICE successor took office, and when the earlier ICE acting period began, were not shown; the TSA report gives no confirmation date or vote. Acting histories for CBP, USCIS, the Coast Guard, CISA and the Secret Service reported by an external retrieval rest on pages that could not be opened and are not relied on. On bills, an external retrieval of Congress.gov and web searches (17 queries, run 2026-10-22; it cannot be reproduced here) found no bill removing Senate confirmation from lower-level DHS posts and none setting a DHS line of succession. It found one general bill, S. 2838 (Protecting Our Democracy Act), introduced 2025-09-17 and referred to the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs with no later action (status record opened on govinfo.gov, 10 cosponsors). That record carries no text or summary, so the external retrieval's report that it amends the Vacancies Act provisions on acting service is unverified, and the bill is not specific to DHS; it is treated as related context and not as a timeline event. The congress.gov search could not be opened here.
